question.leadin: Answer these questions about Japanese history.
question.text: The defeated Ishida said that he fought for the heir of this man. Known by the nicknames of "the monkey" and "the bald rat" because of his looks, his actions included the reunification of Japan and the invasion of Japan.
question.clue: This leader, who initiated construction of Osaka Castle, led failed invasions of Korea in 1592 and 1598.

swap.leadin: Following the failure of the Shimabara Rebellion during this period, Christians were forced underground.
swap.text: Name this last shogunate [show-gun-ate] of Japan. Commodore Matthew Perry entered Japan while this shogunate was in power.
swap.clue: In the later part of this period, known as the Bakumatsu, the Convention of Kanagawa was signed, signaling the reversal of this period's sakoku isolationist policy.

question.text: The battle for this island, home to three Japanese air fields, saw the raising of an American flag on top of its Mount Suribachi.
question.clue: Mass casualties were inflicted on marines during this battle by troops with flamethrowers in a tunnel system that had gone undetected.

swap.leadin: Holders of this title, which originated in the Heian (hay-ahn) period, ruled from the Bakufu.
swap.text: Holding power until the 1867 Meiji (may-jee) Restoration, name this title that denoted military rulers of Japan such as Ashikaga Takauji.
swap.clue: After the arrival of the "black ships," the isolationist rule of this office was ended with the Convention of Kanagawa, shortly before they were made obsolete with the Meiji Restoration.

question.leadin: After travelling 18,000 miles to reach this battle, one side's fleet was destroyed in about a day.
question.text: Name this decisive naval battle fought in 1905 in a namesake strait near Korea. One side was led by Admiral Togo.
question.clue: At the end of this battle, Admiral Nebogatov surrendered rather than doom his 2,000-plus sailors; regardless, his fleet had lost six battleships and twenty-eight other ships in a single day after eight months of sailing from the Baltic Sea.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Meiji Restoration.
swap.text: The Meiji Restoration led to the decline of this warrior class of Japan. Members of this warrior nobility of Japan followed a code of ethics called bushido.
swap.clue: Members of this group could find a job by embarking on a type of pilgrimage called musha shugyo, and their only goal should be "to grasp the long and the short swords and to die".

question.leadin: The first group to hold these titles was known as the shugo, and they included heads of the Hosokawa, Shiba, and Yamana clans.
question.text: Give this feudal title commonly awarded to regional lords in Japan. They typically governed individual provinces under the direction of the shogun.
question.clue: A new aristocratic class known as the kazoku, which worked on a system of hereditary peerage, replaced this noble class following the Meiji Restoration.

swap.leadin: Name the following about U.S. victories in the Pacific theater of World War II.
swap.text: This island with capital of Naha featured the bloodiest battle in the Pacific front, leading many to dub it the "Typhoon of Steel." The Yamato was destroyed on its way to aid in the battle for this island.
swap.clue: This region's Disposition ended its vassalage under the Satsuma Domain established by the Shimazu clan in 1609.

question.leadin: Identify the following historical periods of Japan.
question.text: This period from 1193 to 1333 was begun by the ascension of Yoritomo to the shogunate.
question.clue: The capital was moved from this city to Kyoto during the Kenmu Restoration.

swap.text: This first shogunate began after Minamoto Yoritomo defeated the Tairas at the Battle of Dannoura in 1185. It was dominated by the Hojo family.
swap.clue: Its puppet rulers attempted to revolt with the Jokyu war, but were crushed and remained silent for another century.

question.text: Ieyasu, the commander of the Eastern Army at Sekigahara became shogun in 1603, established this clan of his as rulers of Japan during the Edo Period.
question.clue: One leader with this surname was defeated by Takeda Shingen, but later won a major battle at Nagashino, in alliance with a man who was betrayed and killed by Akechi Mitsuhide, Oda Nobunaga.

swap.leadin: These people were rooted out by having them trample flat icons called fumi-e.
swap.text: Name these people who were forced into hiding following the failed Shimabara Rebellion.
swap.answerHtml: Japanese Christians [accept Catholics; accept Kakure Kirishitan; do not accept or prompt on Protestants or Lutherans or any other branch of Christianity; prompt on just Japanese people]
swap.clue: Twenty of the Twenty-Six Martyrs belonged to this group, whose practices have altered significantly in its "Kakure" incarnation.

question.leadin: Answer the following about aristocratic women in Heian [HAY-on] Japan.
question.text: This work, often called the world's first novel, is an important insight into Heian court life. It features the blank chapter "Vanished into the Clouds" and was written by Lady Murasaki Shikibu.
question.clue: This Heian period work, sometimes called the world's first novel, written by Lady Murasaki.

swap.text: The importance placed on the renunciation of imperial divinity is noted in this 1999 book by John W. Dover that explores the occupation and democratization of Japan after World War II.

question.text: High-fired grey pottery called Sue was introduced by the Gaya Confederacy to Japan during this era of Japanese history, named for its keyhole-shaped tombs.
question.clue: This part of the Yamato period which transitioned to the Asuka period with the introduction of Buddhism to Japan. This Japanese era was named after large keyhole-shaped tombs.

swap.leadin: Ka'en jars, with tops that resemble flames, were principally produced during the middle of this period.
swap.text: Name this period, which gets its name from using rope to make marks on pottery. The Yayoi culture succeeded this period.
swap.clue: This period's namesake hunter-gatherers were supplanted by the agricultural Yayoi ] people.

question.leadin: Emperor Kotoku implemented this set of policies, which included the abolition of private landholding and a tax based on population instead of land use.
question.text: Name this 645 A.D. set of centralizing reforms inspired by Tang Dynasty China, which brought Japan under the control of the imperial court.
question.answerHtml: Taika Reforms [or Taika no Kaishin; or Great Reformation of the Taika Era]
question.clue: The rapid expansion of the Tang and their allies in Korea caused panic in the Japanese imperial court, leading to a palace coup and subsequent political reforms spurred by this set of doctrines issued by Emperor Kotoku in 645.

swap.text: Rusk told Yang that the maritime Macarthur Line would hold until this 1951 treaty took effect. This treaty names the US's "system" of "hub and spokes" bilateral defense treaties with Pacific countries, especially Japan.
swap.answerHtml: Treaty of San Francisco [or San Furanshisuko kōwa-Jōyaku; prompt on Treaty of Peace with Japan or U.S.-Japan Security Treaty (or Japanese equivalents) with “In what city was that treaty signed?]

question.text: The story is often backdated to apply to the rule of this man, who became the first shogun of the Ashikaga shogunate after he'd originally allied with Go-Daigo whom he later turned against.
question.clue: The end of Hojo power came when this warlord overthrew Hojo Takatoki and established himself as shogun in 1336, thus beginning the Muromachi period, which was also known by his clan's name.

swap.leadin: How much do you know about the wild and wooly Sergei Witte, FTPE.
swap.text: Witte was made a count after securing favorable terms for his nation in this treaty ending the Russo-Japanese War.
swap.clue: For brokering this treaty, which the parties signed in Kittery, Maine, U.S. president Theodore Roosevelt received the Nobel Peace Prize.
